Subject: CareTag: initial proposal for HSM/KMS + auditlog billing allocator

Hi Katherine,

Thanks again for the time earlier. Attached is a first pass at packaging and a billing allocator we think will map to CareTag's procurement needs. High-level:

- Implementation/one-time: $120,000 (security onboarding, HSM seat configuration, evidence collection)
- Recurring: audit log retention + KMS seats combined into a per-month line at $6,500/mo
- Proposal uses a 12-month amortization of the implementation credit (you can opt for 24/36 months in the model)

Two compression options we called out in the PDF: per-seat HSM licensing vs throughput-based HSM hours. Both are supported; throughput pricing reduces upfront for pilots but can increase unit cost at scale.

What we need from you to finalize: preferred amortization window (12/24/36), whether procurement requires net-60 PO timing, and any internal cap on one-time fees. If you want, Laura can share a downloadable allocator spreadsheet with numbers split by invoice line.

Attachment: caretag_proposal_v1.pdf (PDF)

Next step: if terms look reasonable, we can draft a short addendum to the SOW that lists the amortization schedule and evidence delivery milestones. We can also convert implementation credit into a monthly credit if that helps your CFO.

Best,

Katherine — thanks for the note. I put together the allocator spreadsheet and two example scenarios; attaching the workbook. Short answers up front: 

- We can apply the implementation amount as a monthly invoice credit (matches your PO reconciliation ask).
- 12-month amortization yields a $10k/mo credit against charges; 36-month yields $3,333/mo. We show both in the model.
- Per-seat HSM (3 seats): we included a seat license of $4,000/month/seat (example) + a $2,000/mo KMS bundle. Throughput alternative: $1,200/month base + $0.0003/op for usage above threshold.

I also added a third column that models a hybrid (1 seat + throughput buffer) — handy for pilots that need a predictable monthly cost but expect variance in calls.

Attachment: billing_allocator_model.xlsx (XLSX)

If procurement wants a lower upfront, we can (a) reduce the implementation invoice and stretch the credit to 24–36 months, or (b) convert the implementation credit to a per-month ‘onboarding support’ credit that invoices against consumption lines. Both are common.

HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DEAL-9876 (for your legal/procurement reference)

Let us know which example you prefer and we will bake it into an addendum draft.

—Laura

Laura/Marissa,

Thanks — the spreadsheet is exactly what procurement needed. A couple of contract-level constraints before we proceed: 

- Our finance team requires a maximum of $40k upfront charge for pilots; anything above must be amortized over at least 24 months.
- PO cadence: we operate on net-45 for new vendors; is net-45 acceptable for the recurring line items?
- We need explicit language stating evidence delivery (SOC 2 Type II report, HIPAA evidence artifacts, HSM attestation logs) will be available within 30 days of SOW effective date.

On HSM licensing: procurement prefers the hybrid approach (1 seat + throughput buffer) for the pilot phase. If we scale to production, we'll switch to per-seat licensing and revisit discounts.

Can you send a one-page addendum that reflects: the hybrid pricing for pilot, onboarding credit amortized at 24 months with monthly invoice credits, and the evidence SLA? Procurement needs that to approve the PO.

Thanks — Katherine

4) Evidence/SLA: we will include a clause in the addendum guaranteeing SOC 2 Type II artifacts and HIPAA evidence delivery within 30 days of SOW effective date; HSM attestation logs will be delivered on the onboarding milestone schedule.
